chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come upon the people wherein their inner secrets will become foul, and their outward appearances will become beautiful, out of greed for the world, not intending by it what is with their Lord. Their religion will be show-off (riya'), with no fear mingling in them. Allah will encompass them with punishment, so they will call out to Him with the supplication of the drowning one, but He will not answer them.'

key_terms.دُعَاءَ الْغَرِيقِ: the supplication of the drowning one

ai.seo_question: What happens to people's faith and prayers when they practice religion for show rather than sincerity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of 'batin' (inner reality) versus 'zahir' (outer appearance), warning that insincerity (riya') corrupts the essence of worship even if the form remains pristine. The metaphor of the 'drowning man's supplication' illustrates the state of spiritual disconnection where external calls for help are ignored due to a lack of internal presence, a theme central to the Purification of the Soul (Tazkiyah).
